title: [codex] Pin GitHub Actions to immutable SHAs
body:
## Summary

Pins every GitHub Actions `uses:` reference in the CI and coverage workflows to a full commit SHA, while leaving the upstream tag or channel as an inline comment for readability.

Fixes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#84.

## Why

The workflows were using mutable action refs such as `@v4`, `@stable`, `@cargo-audit`, and `@v6`. If an action tag or maintainer account were compromised, future workflow runs could execute changed code without a repository diff.

## Latest refs checked

Verified against upstream GitHub refs on 2026-05-07:

- `actions/checkout`: `v6`
- `actions/cache`: `v5`
- `actions/upload-artifact`: `v7`
- `actions/github-script`: `v9`
- `dawidd6/action-download-artifact`: `v21`
- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`: `stable`
- `taiki-e/install-action`: `cargo-audit`, `cargo-llvm-cov`

## Validation

- `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/coverage.yml`
- `ruby -e 'require "yaml"; ARGV.each { |path| YAML.load_file(path); puts "#{path}: ok" }' .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/coverage.yml`
- `perl -ne 'if (/uses:\s*\S+@([^\s#]+)/ && $1 !~ /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/) { print "$ARGV:$.:$1\n"; $bad=1 } END { exit($bad ? 1 : 0) }' .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/coverage.yml`
- Upstream ref comparison for each pinned action SHA
- `git diff --check`
- `just ci`

title: [codex] Fix documented environment variable overrides
body:
## Summary
- preserve the documented `TRANSPONDER_<SECTION>_<KEY>` environment variable format by mapping only the first underscore after the prefix to the section/key boundary
- support comma-separated relay environment variables for `relays.clearnet` and `relays.onion`, and reject JSON-style list input with a clear configuration error
- add regression tests for underscored env keys, env-over-file precedence, relay list parsing, and config test env isolation
- update the README examples to match the supported environment variable behavior

## Why
The root cause was the use of `config::Environment.separator("_")`, which treated every underscore as a hierarchy separator. That caused variables like `TRANSPONDER_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY` to map to `server.private.key` instead of `server.private_key`, so documented env overrides were silently ignored for underscore-containing fields.

## Impact
Operators can now set sensitive values such as `TRANSPONDER_SERVER_PRIVATE_KEY` via environment variables as documented instead of being forced back to config files. Relay env configuration is also explicit and simpler to reason about because it uses comma-separated values.

Fixes marmot-protocol/marmot-security#23.

## Validation
- `cargo test`
- `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified environment-variable naming (first underscore after TRANSPONDER separates section and key) and updated relay examples to use comma-separated lists.

* **Refactor**
  * Environment overrides now apply after loading file defaults; relay variables accept comma-separated values (empty = empty list) and explicitly reject JSON-array formats.

* **Tests**
  * Added tests for env-to-config mapping, file-vs-env precedence, relay parsing, and isolated env handling.

title: [codex] Harden deployment and make Tor support opt-in
body:
## Summary

- harden the Docker and Compose deployment path for production
- add a documented production bundle with optional Caddy/Grafana proxying and firewall guidance
- make Tor relay support opt-in and document the audit policy for optional Tor dependencies

## What changed

- switched the application image to Docker Hardened Images and pinned deploy images by digest
- added a production `compose.prod.yml`, production config/env examples, and a deployment guide
- tightened runtime defaults with non-root execution, read-only filesystems, dropped capabilities, `no-new-privileges`, and secret-file support
- added an internal healthcheck command so health probes do not depend on shell tools in hardened images
- added `cargo audit` workflow support, a local `just audit` wrapper, and CI coverage for the optional Tor feature
- gated onion relay support behind `--features tor` and reject onion relay config in the default build

## Why

We wanted a concrete production deployment path before bringing up a server, while keeping the default footprint smaller and making the optional Tor path an explicit operator choice. The audit wrapper documents the remaining upstream Tor-only advisories without weakening the default build.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`
- `cargo check --features tor`
- `cargo test --features tor test_relay_client_allows_onion_relays_with_tor_feature -- --nocapture`
- `just audit`

title: fix: implement bounded queue in PushDispatcher to prevent DoS
body:
## Summary

- Implements bounded queue pattern to prevent unbounded task spawning (DoS vulnerability)
- Replaces immediate task spawning with a fixed-size mpsc channel (10,000 capacity)
- Uses 4 worker tasks to process the queue and send notifications
- Drops new notifications when queue is full to protect against OOM

## Problem

The `dispatch()` function was spawning a new Tokio task for every notification immediately. While the semaphore limited concurrent *executing* pushes to 100, there was no limit on *spawned tasks* waiting for permits. Under heavy load, this could cause unbounded memory growth and OOM crashes.

## Solution

Use Option 1 from the issue: bounded mpsc channel with drop-on-overload semantics.

- `MAX_PENDING_QUEUE_SIZE = 10,000` - bounds memory usage
- `NUM_WORKERS = 4` - processes queue concurrently
- `try_send()` used to avoid blocking; logs warning if queue full
- Graceful shutdown signals workers before waiting for completion

## Testing

- All existing tests pass
- Added new tests for queue behavior and shutdown handling
- Code coverage maintained (90.36% lines vs 90.28% baseline)

Closes #19

title: Add LRU cache with size limit for event deduplication
body:
## Summary

- Replace unbounded HashMap with LRU cache to prevent memory exhaustion during high event volume or attack conditions
- Add configurable `max_dedup_cache_size` option (default: 100,000 entries)
- Add comprehensive tests for LRU eviction behavior

## Details

The event deduplication cache (`seen_events`) could grow unbounded between cleanup cycles (60 seconds). Under high event volume, this could lead to excessive memory usage before the periodic cleanup task runs.

This PR replaces the HashMap with an LRU cache that automatically evicts the least recently used entries when the configured size limit is reached. The existing time-based cleanup (5-minute expiration) is preserved for stale entry removal.

## Configuration

The cache size is configurable via:

```toml
[server]
max_dedup_cache_size = 100000
```

Or via environment variable:

```bash
TRANSPONDER_SERVER_MAX_DEDUP_CACHE_SIZE=100000
```

title: Add retry logic for transient push notification failures
body:
## Summary

- Implements retry with exponential backoff for 429 (rate limiting) and 5xx (server errors)
- Adds new `retry` module with configurable retry behavior
- Both APNs and FCM clients now automatically retry transient failures

## Details

Previously, transient failures like rate limiting (429) or server errors (5xx) would silently drop notifications without any retry attempt. This could cause legitimate notifications to be permanently lost during temporary service issues.

### Changes

**New retry module (`src/push/retry.rs`):**
- `RetryConfig` with configurable max retries (default: 3) and initial backoff (default: 100ms)
- `SendAttemptResult` enum distinguishing between success, retriable, and permanent errors
- Exponential backoff with maximum cap of 10 seconds
- Retry-After header parsing support

**APNs client:**
- 429 responses now trigger retry with Retry-After header support
- 5xx responses now trigger retry
- 400, 403, 410 remain non-retriable (permanent failures per spec)

**FCM client:**
- Same retry behavior as APNs
- 400, 401, 404 remain non-retriable

title: Remove APNs certificate-based authentication
body:
## Summary

- Removes certificate-based authentication for APNs entirely (token-based JWT auth only)
- Removes `auth_method`, `certificate_path`, and `certificate_password` config options
- Improves test coverage for push clients and relay handling

## Problem

Certificate-based authentication was advertised as supported but not actually implemented. When configured, requests would go out without any authentication, causing 403 errors. The server would report as healthy via `/ready` but silently fail to deliver all iOS push notifications.

## Solution

Rather than implementing full mTLS support (which requires significant work), this PR removes certificate auth entirely. Token-based (JWT) authentication is the modern standard recommended by Apple and is already fully implemented.

**Breaking change**: Users with `auth_method = "certificate"` in their config will need to switch to token-based auth.
